done.why: I read enough to judge the prose and stopped early. I didn't try the puzzles or reach an ending.

about: A Zork-style underground empire. You enter a barrow with a lantern and sword and cross a ravine into a cavern and garden. A Wizard taunts you and makes illusions, and treasures are hidden further south.

moments.note: The lantern description says it has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
Turning on the lamp summons the Wizard, who reads your empty hands and tells you where the treasure is.
Taking the illusory jewels fails with a line saying the room looks embarrassed.
The room settles down once the illusion fades.

wished: Wanted to go on to the stone door and the room that will not keep still.

lines.line: He peers at you from under his bushy eyebrows, as though you were not at all what he had been expecting, and had turned up anyway.
lines.why: Gives the Wizard character in one sentence.

lines.line: the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: A funny, original way to refuse an action.

fun.why: Familiar map with a witty narrator on top.

engagement.why: The Wizard's hints about the pearls and the shifting room made me want to go on.

difficulty.why: I barely met any obstacles in the time I played.

interestingness.why: It reworks classic Zork places with new reactive details such as the illusions.

prose.why: The added descriptions are dry and witty. They sit well beside the original room text.
